title: How this model works
summary: A competitiveness rating for every team in college football, updated weekly and scored against what actually happened.
html:
This is an attempt to create a comprehensive competitiveness comparison between teams at all levels (FBS, FCS, D2, D3, NAIA; Also, JC and U-Sports). This should be comparable to Bill Connelly's expanded rankings that he posts weekly during the season, but using my own methodology. The results of my model are displayed in the views on this website, which are split up into Scoreboard, CCS, Team, Sandbox, and Model Accuracy.

Scoreboard

This section is simple and exactly how it sounds. The scores of the week, as well as the model projections, will populate after the game is played. The schedule for each week is always displayed for the purpose of ranking all games based on an "Interest" score, which weighs games based on closeness in skill and quality of play. I have not added in a rivalry component, but once I find a good place that holds all rivalries, I'll get that component added.

CCS (Competitiveness Composite Score)

The CCS section is split up into four views: Pre-Season, In-Season, Post-Season, Off-Season. These splits are all interconnected. The Off-Season look pulls from the end point of the previous season, makes some adjustments based on roster turnover, coaching changes, etc. and produces the Pre-Season rankings. The Pre-Season rankings are the starting point for the In-Season rankings, the In-Season rankings project the Post-Season setup, the end point then flows into the next Off-Season. The primary purpose of these dashboards are to show the power rankings and record adjusted rankings by team and conference, and display projected W/L totals for the whole season and in-conference.

Each display is mostly unique, Pre-Season and In-Season are somewhat the same view, where Pre-Season is stagnant for the beginning of the year and In-Season will update with each week of games. Selecting a team will bring up the teams projected record statistics. Off-Season is a truncated view of the Pre/In-Season view, but instead of seeing a teams projected record, selecting a team will show the Off-Season gains and losses based on roster movement, coaching change, roster talent adjustments, etc. The final view is the Post-Season, which is the unique view amongth the four dashboards. The Post-Season dashboard projects conference championships, auto-qualifiers, playoff seeding, and final outcomes. It is still a work in progress (the ACC situation last year really pushed the boundaries of the playoff seeding system). Once I come up with a good workaround for that, the playoff picture will update properly each week.

Team

This section is a breakdown of the wins and losses for each team by season. It shows the progress of the team's CCS each week, the games that hurt/helped the score the most, and a re-display of the off-season summary. I am currently working on a detailed version of the talent component that shows position group changes as well, which I think will add a more detailed element for the off-season talent shift.

Sandbox

Sandbox is the catch all for projects currently under heavy testing and building, but still deserve to be displayed. Right now, I am tracking coaching changes and performance here. I am working through a synergy model theory that incorporates talent building, play style, and complimentary football. There are a few additional performance pieces, such as ability to close, drive success, etc. that I am also formulating. Right now, the sandbox has an overall coaching view by season and a team level coaching view by season. The team level view attempts to split out the offense and deffense success rates; however, the source play by play data is messy, so any errors are still being fixed.

Model Accuracy

This section is important for tracking how well the model projections perform against actual results. It's mostly a way of being transparent about the model and allowing me to see where there are any shortcomings that I can improve on.
